priority: ADR-023 — we prioritise HIGH CERTAINTY over HIGH DETECTION: specificity at the op-point is the criterion, recall is a constraint to satisfy, and MAE ranks nothing. A low recall here is usually the choice working. Read spec first, and read recall beside the positive rate.

caveats: NOT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE PREVIOUS CHECKPOINT. Every #95 band overlaps with the epoch-4 model's (recall, precision, specificity, F1). The point estimates all move adversely -- precision 0.706 -> 0.550, specificity 0.9920 -> 0.9856, FP 5 -> 9 -- and under the owner's 2026-08-06 rule two models whose bands overlap are not distinguishable whatever their point estimates say. Do not report the change as a regression, and do not report it as an improvement.

THE PRECISION DROP IS MOSTLY BOUNDARY DISAGREEMENT, NOT JUNK. Classified by the oracle's own scope_verdict, 6 of the 9 false positives are `in_scope` -- articles the oracle calls thriving stories, scored just under 4.5, which the student put just over. Genuinely off-lens is 3 of 20 (off-lens precision 0.850 vs the old 0.882) and category errors (harm_is_subject) are 1, the SAME as the old checkpoint. ⚠️ These are counts of 17 and 20 articles; '1 vs 1' compares two single articles, not two rates.

⛔ DO NOT SET THIS RECALL BESIDE THE FLEET'S 0.59-0.72. v7 and v8 do not share a positive class -- Jaccard 0.246 on these same rows. Two recalls of two different classes are two quantities with one name.

SAMPLE, NOT POPULATION. The 660 rows are a 25.1x design-weighted draw (inclusion_probability in datasets/scored/human_thriving_v8/corpus.jsonl). Every rate here is unweighted and describes the SPLIT. Production rates must be measured from production output after deploy.
